description:
I'M focused on developing innovative space exploration and satellite concepts, integrating advanced optics, hardware systems, and satellite architectures to address complex challenge statements.

Team Members: Working alongside Reza Ghadimi (AI & Software Developer) and Sanitha Sudevan. (Data Acquisition Specialist) to build an integrated space solution.
summary: SPHEREx maps the entire sky every six months in 102 near-infrared bands, producing an enormous volume of data. Moving objects such as asteroids, brown dwarfs, and nearby stars reveal themselves through positional shifts between epochs. However, part of this apparent motion is caused by Earth’s orbital parallax, which complicates accurate detection. ParallaxStack is a public-facing web tool designed to address this challenge. Users enter sky coordinates (RA, Dec), and the system retrieves multi-epoch SPHEREx images, applies parallax-aware alignment, and provides temporal visualization along with difference imaging and simple stacking modes. This approach helps separate real moving objects from background stars and makes faint movers easier to detect. The tool is tested on key targets suggested by NASA, including WISE 0855 and Barnard’s Star.
details: What It Does & How It Works: ParallaxStack is an open-source multi-epoch astronomical image analyzer designed to detect moving celestial objects and solve the parallax effect in NASA SPHEREx near-infrared sky survey data. Users upload multi-epoch astronomical image cubes (including FITS files), and the tool processes them through image alignment, background subtraction, and difference imaging to highlight subtle positional shifts over time. It also includes basic stacking capabilities to boost the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for faint transient or moving targets, outputting detected sources and motion tracks in CSV and JSON formats. Benefits & Intended Impact: Analyzing multi-epoch infrared sky surveys typically requires complex, resource-heavy pipelines. ParallaxStack streamlines this workflow into a lightweight, fast, and accessible local web interface. By making parallax solving and transient detection straightforward, it empowers researchers, students, and citizen scientists to explore deep-space datasets efficiently and contribute to open-science discoveries. Tools & Technologies Used: - Programming Language: Python 3 - Libraries & Frameworks: NumPy (for array and image matrix calculations), Astropy (for FITS file handling and World Coordinate System/WCS support), and Python's built-in HTTP server for the lightweight local web interface. - Cross-Platform Compatibility: Designed to run seamlessly on both desktop environments (Windows/Streamlit) and mobile devices (Android via Pydroid). Creativity & Key Considerations: Instead of relying on heavy cloud servers, ParallaxStack was engineered to be lightweight enough to run locally even on mobile hardware while still handling scientific FITS data cubes. Additionally, we considered global accessibility by incorporating a bilingual interface (English and Persian/Farsi) directly into the application, lowering language barriers for aspiring space data analysts.
